rationale: Manual authoring after v0009 still failed t38 at 46% and t40 at 48% in run 20260523-185835. v0009 fixed the prior 'rank sub-clusters and keep the strongest' failure mode by adding the disjoint-sub-cluster union rule (rule 5) and rewriting rule 6 so 'one hit' allows multi-actor MOs. The new failure mode is upstream of those rules: the Executor's impossible-travel signal is implemented with `haversine(observed_lat, observed_lon)` (actor-side coords) instead of `haversine(stores.lat, stores.lon)` (claimed-entity coords joined via store_id). The dev benchmark's fraud cohorts contain two MOs per hit: (a) paired-travel — N customers each making two payments 200-500 km apart in minutes, the actor's observed coords genuinely move; (b) stationary-burst — one customer makes 10+ payments at 10+ stores in 2-4 minutes while observed coords stay constant and store_id rotates across distant cities. The observed-axis sweep catches MO (a) but returns 0 km for MO (b). The store-axis sweep catches both. In the failing run t39 happened to use store coords and scored 100%; t38 and t40 used observed coords and scored 46-48%, recovering exactly the paired-travel half of each cohort. The signal-families table in v0009 names 'geographic separation (impossible travel)' without specifying which axis; the choice is stochastic across trials. Fix is surgical: (a) expand rule 2's Time/sequence row to require sweeping BOTH location axes (actor-side observed AND claimed-entity-side stored) and unioning the results, with the worked example explaining why stationary-burst MOs require the store axis; (b) add a 'density refinement' paragraph to rule 4 saying a high-count threshold signal (50+, 100+, 200+) is not automatically noise — regroup by (actor, short-time-window) and look at per-group densities before dismissing, since bursts can hide inside the continuous distribution; (c) add a 'temporal scoping' paragraph to rule 6 saying 'one hit' implies one connected 1-3 week window, so sub-clusters separated by 4+ weeks are separate incidents (addresses the t40 false-positive observed in my analytical solve: a 3-record sub-cluster on 2021-06-12 sits 5 weeks after the main 2021-05-06 hit and is excluded by the grader); (d) extend rule 7 coverage-check with three new line items: record which axes were swept for parameterised signals, record density-by-actor distribution for high-count threshold signals, record temporal span when the brief says 'one hit'; (e) add three new anti-patterns: single-axis-only impossible-travel, dismissing high-count threshold without density refinement, mixing sub-clusters from multiple temporal windows when the brief says 'one hit'. No language is benchmark-specific — every rule names the abstract pattern (location axis, threshold density, temporal connectedness) with column names as illustrative. The fix complements v0009 instead of replacing it: disjoint-sub-cluster union (v0009 rule 5) still applies once the signal correctly finds all sub-clusters. v0009's discrete > fuzzy rule (rule 4) still holds; density refinement is a sub-rule that runs before dismissing the fuzzy signal, not after.

rollback.strategy: Revert to v0009 by creating a new version from v0009 content if the new multi-axis sweep / density refinement / temporal scoping rules cause regressions on tasks where (a) only one location axis is meaningful in the schema (the multi-axis paragraph then asks for a sweep that is structurally impossible), or (b) the brief actually intends multiple temporally-distant hits as one cohort and the temporal-scoping anti-pattern wrongly trims them. The narrow rollback is dropping the temporal-scoping paragraph from rule 6 and its matching anti-pattern, keeping the multi-axis and density-refinement edits which target the t38/t40 under-recall path.
